biological.citation: NUP85 alleviates lipid metabolism and inflammation by regulating PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (PMID: 38617542)
biological.summary: NUP85 regulates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and interacts with CCR2 to modulate lipid metabolism and inflammation in NAFLD. NUP85 knockdown decreased fat disorder and inflammation levels in MCD-induced mice and FFA-stimulated AML-12 cells, while ISRIB (NUP85 inhibitor) alleviated NAFLD.

biological.citation: NUP85 siRNA loaded red blood cell-derived extracellular vesicles alleviate hepatic steatosis in MASLD (PMID: 41413582)
biological.summary: NUP85 promotes lipid accumulation in hepatocytes via the SLC27A1/PPAR-γ signaling pathway. Serum NUP85 levels are significantly elevated in MASLD patients and correlate with disease severity. RBC-EVs@siNUP85 delivery system effectively silenced NUP85 in hepatocytes, alleviating hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in both in vitro and in vivo models.

biological.citation: NUP85 as a Neurodevelopmental Gene: From Podocyte to Neuron (PMID: 38136965)
biological.summary: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants (c.611T>A, p.Val204Glu and c.1904T>G, p.Leu635Arg) cause steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with severe neurodevelopmental impairment including microcephaly, axial hypotonia, seizures, corpus callosum hypoplasia, and simplified cerebral cortex gyration, expanding NUP85's role beyond renal function to brain development.

NUP85 mutations cause autosomal recessive steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome with median onset at 7 years and progression to kidney failure at median age 8.5 years. Kidney biopsies reveal focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in 89% of patients. Extrarenal manifestations include neurological, growth/development, cardiovascular disorders, and congenital malformations.

biological.citation: Docking a flexible basket onto the core of the nuclear pore complex (PMID: 39138317)
biological.summary: NUP85 is a subunit of the Y-complex of the nuclear pore complex that interacts with basket subunit Nup60 through a tripartite junction involving short linear motifs. This interaction couples transcription to mRNA quality control and export, and was validated through AlphaFold-based screens, electron microscopy, membrane-templated reconstitution, and in vivo validation.

biological.citation: An Arabidopsis Nucleoporin NUP85 modulates plant responses to ABA and salt stress (PMID: 29232718)
biological.summary: Arabidopsis NUP85 mutants exhibit reduced expression of stress-responsive genes (RD29A, COR15A, COR47) in response to ABA and salt stress. NUP85 associates with HOS1 and other nucleoporins within the nup107-160 complex and directly interacts with mediator subunit MED18, linking the nuclear pore complex to mediator complex in stress gene regulation.

biological.citation: Analysis of correlation between high expression of nucleoporin 85 (NUP85) and immune cell infiltration in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 38952090)
biological.summary: NUP85 mRNA and protein are upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma across different stages and grades, with 19% mutation rate significantly affecting overall survival, disease-specific survival, and progression-free survival. NUP85 is highly expressed in macrophages, B cells, and T cells and positively correlates with immune cell infiltration. GO/KEGG enrichment shows NUP85 co-expressed genes are enriched in cell cycle and chromosome segregation pathways.

biological.citation: Deficient chaperone-mediated autophagy in macrophage aggravates inflammation of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis by targeting Nup85 (PMID: 36912786)
biological.summary: Nup85 functions as a substrate for chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) in macrophages. CMA dysfunction in hepatic macrophages impairs Nup85 degradation, aggravating monocyte recruitment and promoting liver inflammation and fibrosis in NASH. Inhibition of Nup85 attenuated steatosis and monocyte recruitment caused by CMA deficiency in NASH mice.

biological.citation: Case report: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants cause autosomal recessive primary microcephaly (PMID: 36846113)
biological.summary: Compound heterozygous NUP85 variants cause primary autosomal recessive microcephaly without steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome or Seckel syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum. Patient-derived fibroblasts showed reduced cell viability, and structural simulation predicted the variants alter NUP85 structure and interactions with neighboring nucleoporins.
biological.sample_size: 1 index patient plus 1 additional unrelated individual

biological.citation: Nucleoporin 85 interacts with influenza A virus PB1 and PB2 to promote its replication by facilitating nuclear import of ribonucleoprotein (PMID: 36051755)
biological.summary: NUP85 interacts with influenza A virus polymerase subunits PB1 and PB2 in an RNA-dependent manner to facilitate nuclear import of viral ribonucleoprotein. NUP85 knockdown delayed vRNP nuclear import and suppressed viral replication. NUP85 assists binding of PB1 to RanBP5 and PB2 to importin α1/α7, and NUP85 expression is downregulated upon IAV infection.

biological.citation: NUP85 Mediates Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress through the USP47/ASK1 Signaling Pathway to Regulate the Progression of Liver Fibrosis (PMID: 41903125)
biological.summary: NUP85 is elevated in liver fibrosis and regulates the USP47/ASK1 signaling pathway. NUP85 competitively binds USP47 to deubiquitinate ASK1 at lysine 805, exacerbating endoplasmic reticulum stress and collagen deposition. NUP85 knockdown ameliorated liver injury and fibrosis, while overexpression promoted pathological changes. CREKA-coupled liposomes delivered Mogroside V (NUP85 inhibitor) to attenuate fibrosis.
